title: New Relic VS Sentry (FE/Browser and session monitoring)
content:
Purpose of this document is to understand the key differences between NR and Sentry when it comes to front end monitoring, browser monitoring and user session monitoring. Recently we have conducted an evaluation using Ordna planner , where we have introduced NR (Sentry is already used by Ordna) and enabled user session monitoring and error tracking.

Document ends with recommendations .

High-level difference between NewRelic and Sentry

NewRelic

Sentry

Comments

Application Performance management tool. All in one APM that enable end to end monitoring starting from downstream end user till upstream lines of code .

This is a platform for workflow productivity , focused on aggregating errors across the stack in real time. Provides code level context to resolve issues at various stage of application lifecycle.

Performance monitoring

Primarily exception monitoring

Key features:

  • Performance data retention

  • Response time at each layer, throughput etc

  • breakdown of performance by component, by layer

  • Cross platform visibility and distributed tracing.

  • Mapping performance data to end user experience.

  • error and user session monitoring

  • Easy setup, really powerful and superior visualization are the reasons why developers use NR.

Key features:

  • Real time updates on exception . Developers can fix code level issues anywhere in the stack before it leaks as user errors.

  • Complete context: spend more time where it matters , rather than investing in low impact issues.

  • Drop-in integration for major platforms, frameworks and language. Easy to integrate.

  • Consolidates similar errors and makes resolution easy", "Email Notifications" and "Open source integrations" are the primary reasons why Sentry is favored.

License model is usage and role centric. Different stake holders can have different license type (roles defined in ADs and NR) based on need and usage. https://docs.newrelic.com/docs/accounts/accounts-billing/new-relic-one-pricing-billing/new-relic-one-pricing-billing/

As open source as possible. Minimal difference between Sentry SaaS and Self hosted offerings.

Projects teams needs to do more analysis on cost and license type.

Key findings are listed below in the table:

key monitoring areas and data visualization

Sentry

New Relic

Comments

  1. Breadcrumbs (https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/enriching-events/breadcrumbs/ )for sending meaningful data for analysis.

  2. Timeline of event by looking at bugs and errors

  • Yes, this option is quite dynamic in Sentry.

  • Option to filter required data and send events based on demand

  • Option to filter out duplicates

  • NR version is “Session timeline app capability“

  • New Relic has a custom OSS NROne app (It’s open source https://opensource.newrelic.com/nerdpacks/ the app is “Browser Analyzer”) that can visualize all
    events generated by a specific user in a browser session.

  • Summarized golden metrics
    ● An event stream of all events triggered by a specific user session
    ● A distribution of events alone a gauge showing total elapsed time
    ● A drilldown showing all attributes recorded for each event in the event stream
    ● Ability to filter the event stream to view only events of a specific category
    ● Ability to define performance thresholds for specific event types and flag events that
    breach those thresholds

Key difference between Sentry and NR is the amount of customization and ease of use. Sentry has easy access to breadcrumbs and can be customized faster, but at the same NR provides truck load of information which gives relatively better insights but needs analysis.

Support for intercepting events

usecases:

  1. filtering of errors of a certain type

  2. sending events to insights , used to calculate conversion rates caused by degraded performance

  3. adding more information to events

  • Ability to filter out errors based on interest and frequency of occurrence.

  • possibility of using regex to filter errors.

  • configuration option available on a sentry plugin in client side. Makes filtering easy.

  • Filter out completely all errors of a specific type by using SPA API. For custom er
    filtering of errors to include only a subset of occurrences the suggested method of Nerdgraph drop rules. https://docs.newrelic.com/docs/data-apis/manage-data/drop-data-using-nerdgraph/

  • New Relic Errors Inbox helps you with grouped errors based on attributes and fingerprint
    collected. More details about error grouping is below.

  • You can curate an Error Inbox specific to a team’s focus entities by creating a workload
    and configuring an Error’s Inbox for that workload. https://docs.newrelic.com/docs/errors-inbox/errors-inbox/#get-started

  • There was also an ask to a centralized Errors Inbox that shows the errors of all the
    planner, this can easily be done by configuring an Errors Inbox in master account level with users
    having access to multiple accounts.

The browser and Single Page Application (SPA) APIs allow you to customize and extend your browser monitoring. To begin using the APIs, ensure the browser JavaScript snippet is present on every page you want to monitor.

https://docs.newrelic.com/docs/browser/new-relic-browser/guides/guide-using-browser-spa-apis/#api-errors

Too much performance data all of which is not necessary and not useful

  • Perhaps it’s also caused by a missing concept of page navigation for SPA in new relic.

  • E.g. how can I find performance problem after the planner has been loaded when user
    navigates between different pages in a single page application ?

  • How can I find out if a certain page has degraded performance ?
    How can I measure how long time it takes to load a page and the spinner is gone (the 3D engine
    is ready)

In Sentry it’s possible to cover the areas mentioned in the requirement of monitoring an SPA.

New Relic feedback:

  • New Relic browser monitoring has a single-page application (SPA) monitoring feature that
    provides deeper visibility and actionable insights into real user interactions with single-page apps.
    SPA data monitored by browser monitoring includes:

  • Performance data and throughput for page loads and route changes

  • AJAX request data

  • JavaScript activity, both synchronous and asynchronous

  • Dynamic page updates, monitored using the SPA API. https://docs.newrelic.com/docs/browser/single-page-app-monitoring/get-started/introduction-single-page-app-monitoring/

  • Page load->Spinner: Record spinner actions as a custom event using https://docs.newrelic.com/docs/browser/new-relic-browser/guides/guide-using-browser-spa-apis/#api-traces the agent
    can pickup this custom timing for you.

  • Alternatively you can also use Simple Browser/Scripted Browser Synthetic monitor to navigate the spinner and log the duration.

Automatic support for reading Source maps

possible

The recommended method other than upload the Souce Maps via the UI is to use the API method.

https://docs.newrelic.com/docs/browser/new-relic-browser/browser-pro-features/upload-source-maps-api

Grouping of errors and mechanism of filtering relevant errors by category

  • Merge errors in Sentry UI manually which is a handy feature

  • sentry also allows to change the algorithm how hashes are generated to provide a better grouping
    of issues.

  • For example, by only including 3 level deep stack traces or exclude stacktrace items coming form
    kompis. Also, sometimes you want to provide a hash for an error on the client side when you manually trigger or throw
    an exception in your code to make sure all of those errors are grouped correctly.

  • Drill down on errors to find more stats. e.g country, region, browser, version , unique users affected, create dashboard widget for unique issues etc.

  • Errors inbox is a single place to proactively detect, triage, and take action on all the errors before they impact users / customers.

  • Error grouping : How it works

    • Error events get grouped into an error group when they share the same fingerprint. As events are
      ingested by New Relic, it runs the events through a set of managed rules that output a fingerprint.
      Every unique fingerprint has a single error group associated with it.
      The New Relic managed rules normalize the error data, identifying and ignoring unique values such as UUIDs, hex values, email addresses, etc. that would cause grouping “like” errors into unique groups. NR account ID, entity ID, error class, error message, stack trace and exception are all data that can impact a fingerprint.

  • https://docs.newrelic.com/docs/errors-inbox/errors-inbox/#error-details

  • Versioning : As part of Sourcemap upload, add the regression tag (https://docs.newrelic.com/docs/errors-inbox/errors-inbox/#regression-tag ) so errors attributes can be enriched to include versions.

  • Errors Inbox UI encourages collaboration within the tool allowing you to assign
    owners, comment on the error tab so as to encourage cross dev collaboration and the error data is persistent, so if an error that has been worked on or resolved, crops up again, you can see the full history of the work done it from before.

  • NR team is working on adding functionality to be able to group errors by
    unique users in the coming month. However you can today send custom attributes( user id maybe) to understand error trends for unique users.

The configuration of newrelic and the newrelic SPA API feels limiting
e.g. how to filter bots, browser plugin crashes, old browsers” In sentry UI there is a page where you can,

  • Filter out errors known to be caused by browser extensions

  • Filter out known errors from legacy browsers

  • Filter out known web crawlers

  • Or custom filters, e.g. a release version, ip address, error message

In NR , use the attributes functionality( eg: UserAgent attribute and IPaddress) in Errors Inbox to filter out legacy browsers, browser extensions and custom filters.

custom filters, e.g. a release
version, ip address, error message.
For web crawlers and bots UseCases, you can use NRQL queries to do chart them in a dashboard.

https://discuss.newrelic.com/t/any-advice-on-how-to-filter-bots-out-of-insights-dashboards/99541

The NR monitor summary page does not give much value, In new relic we only see data for the page load.

  • would like to see performance data for each single page in the single page application.

  • Also useful is user misery (Misery counts the number of unique users who were frustrated based on four times the satisfactory response time threshold (ms).)

Possible in Sentry

  • The best way to explore how the New Relic UI would be a custom demo(happy to bring specific planner team through that) or a read through https://docs.newrelic.com/docs/browser/single-page-app-monitoring/use-spa-data/view-spa-data-browser-ui/ which is good compact guide of the experience.

  • Apdex score: New Relic calls ‘user misery’ as Apdex score. Its the same concept. See https://docs.newrelic.com/docs/apm/new-relic-apm/apdex/apdex-measure-user-satisfaction/ for details.

Page navigation in an SPA

react development , sentry makes it easy with various integrations ,

For SPAs it’s more useful .

Recommendations:

  • As the cost of usage will vary based on team of different sizes and delivery model, we recommend New Relic for applications falling under complex architecture for better tracing and monitoring. It is quite obvious that Sentry will be cheaper due to the smaller set of focus area as compared to NewRelic.

  • Sentry is recommended for projects and developers only focused on exception monitoring, error handling and code level tracing. But if the need is better visibility and distributed tracing (together with exception handling and end user session monitoring) we recommend New Relic.

  • We recommend New Relic for projects having business models which demand higher Data curiosity (based on SLAs and NFRs on IT operational level) for an entire team , taking ownership of the delivery and environments.

  • Based on the evaluations, discussions and analysis we recommend NewRelic as the preferred solution due the below mentioned KEY points (barring cost of usage)

    • Better observability

    • Better cross platform/service tracing

    • can be used as IPEX ONE solution for all

    • Helps in building a COE or core team which can act as enablers .

    • Helps with future changes in project ownerships which might demand higher DATA curiosity. Data retention is better.

    • Infra as code (e.g: terraform integration ) which can help better onboarding and configuration
